name: Experimental Design Checklist
description: This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any experimental design task, implementation, or piece of work complete.
content:
This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any experimental design task, implementation, or piece of work complete.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. State assumptions about experimental design explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
2. When experimental design guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
3. Re-check edge cases relevant to experimental design (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
4. Prefer explicit, readable experimental design solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
5. Keep experimental design outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
6. When experimental design decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
7. Prefer the simplest experimental design approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
8. Keep experimental design changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
9. Check that experimental design terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
10. Before starting experimental design work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
11. Document any non-obvious experimental design decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
12. When multiple experimental design strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of experimental design correctness.
- Do not apply generic experimental design advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid introducing new experimental design abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these experimental design guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
